prospects.thesis: LHX is the top-ranked prospect with the strongest composite score, combining bullish options flow and institutional accumulation with a reasonable 2.2x P/S. The company's communications, electronic warfare, and space systems portfolio is benefiting from elevated DoD budgets and allied rearmament cycles, while its Aerojet Rocketdyne integration is driving solid rocket motor demand amid munitions restocking. The +16.7% monthly move reflects smart money positioning ahead of continued FY27 budget tailwinds.

RTX offers large-cap diversification across Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon, with bullish options and institutional signals confirming the setup. The GTF engine issue is largely in the rearview, while Patriot, LTAMDS, and NGJ missile/air-defense backlogs continue expanding on global demand. A more modest +10.8% monthly move versus peers suggests less extended entry with meaningful room to rerate.

HII provides unique exposure to naval shipbuilding (Virginia-class subs, Ford-class carriers) — a sub-niche with essentially monopolistic positioning and multi-decade visibility tied to AUKUS and Pacific deterrence priorities. At 0.9x P/S with bullish institutional flow and +18.1% monthly momentum, the market is finally recognizing margin recovery and improved shipyard throughput. Entry here captures a structurally underappreciated defense prime.

SAIC gives us defense IT services exposure — a distinct sub-niche from the primes — focused on digital engineering, mission IT, and AI integration for DoD and intelligence customers. At 0.9x P/S with bullish institutional positioning and +20.3% monthly momentum, the stock is riding the Pentagon's software/AI modernization budget while trading at a discount to hardware peers. Fits our AI + Defense theme crossover cleanly.

KTOS is the pure-play on unmanned systems (Valkyrie, tactical drones) and hypersonics targets — a high-growth sub-niche distinct from traditional primes and tied directly to CCA (Collaborative Combat Aircraft) program wins. Bullish options and institutional signals support the thesis, but the -2.6% monthly pullback versus sector strength warrants a disciplined entry rather than chasing. The 5.1x P/S reflects growth premium, so timing matters.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into the cyclical, pro-growth corners of the market — Industrials (lit up like a Christmas tree at 8x normal volume), Consumer Discretionary, Communications, and Financials — which is a classic "the economy is going to run hot" bet, likely fueled by expectations around infrastructure spending follow-through, defense appropriations, deregulation tailwinds for banks, and the possibility that tariff policy actually benefits domestic manufacturers more than it hurts them. On the flip side, the smart money is quietly running for the exits in the defensive and rate-sensitive stuff: Consumer Staples is showing an absolutely absurd put/call ratio of 8.78 (someone is making a massive bet that Coke, Procter & Gamble and friends are heading lower), Utilities and Real Estate are getting hedged as traders price in "higher rates for longer," and Healthcare's heavy bearish flow smells like positioning around drug pricing pressure, Medicare negotiation headlines, and uncertainty over HHS policy direction.
